clue.text: Cheerful bishop's flexible

parts.note: B is the chess abbreviation for bishop
lithe means supple, bending easily

explanation.surface: A jolly clergyman who is also limber, perhaps from yoga.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's stands for 'is', joining the definition to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Blithe is a slightly literary synonym for happy and carefree.

clue.text: Comic strip character, a valet

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the caped crusader of DC comics
second meaning: an army officer's personal servant

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a cartoon butler; the comma separates two unrelated senses.
explanation.definitionFit: The superhero and the military orderly who looks after an officer share one name.

clue.text: Stupid, one point put about one in charge

parts.note: the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: something put about another thing surrounds it, so one piece is placed around another

parts.note: a dot is a small point
the Roman numeral again, placed inside the point
IC is the standard abbreviation for in charge

explanation.surface: Someone dismissing a silly move made by a person in authority.
explanation.walkthrough: The second 'one' goes inside the point: D(I)OT.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiotic is a direct synonym of stupid, both meaning foolish or senseless.

clue.text: Girl's broken heel close to pavilion

indicators.note: something broken is smashed apart, so its letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the close of a word is its end, so only its final letter is kept

parts.note: the last letter of pavilion

explanation.surface: A girl snaps the heel of her shoe near the cricket pavilion.
explanation.definitionFit: Helen is a common girl's name, so it is an example of the definition.

clue.text: Get down to nudism, astonishingly

indicators.note: an astonishing outcome is a wild one, so the letters are thrown into a surprising new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone surprisingly turns to naturism, getting down to it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Get down to' reads as one phrase, but 'to' belongs to the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: To dismount is to get down from a horse or bicycle.

clue.text: Behind bars having committed swindle — judge intolerant

indicators.note: to commit is to put someone away, so one piece is placed within another that has taken it in

parts.note: inside is slang for in prison
a con is a trick or swindle
to rate is to assess or judge

explanation.surface: A prisoner jailed for fraud complains the judge was harsh.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Committed' is meant in the prison sense of being sent down, so the swindle is placed in the middle of the word for jailed.
explanation.definitionFit: An inconsiderate person shows no patience or regard for others, close in sense to being intolerant.

clue.text: Rough and ready model needing dress

parts.note: a make is a model or brand, as of a car
a shift is a simple straight dress

explanation.surface: A fashion model, unprepared, urgently needs something to wear.
explanation.definitionFit: Something makeshift is improvised and crude, serving temporarily as a rough-and-ready substitute.

clue.text: Excavate part of chateau near there

indicators.note: only a part of the following words is wanted, so the solution sits inside a run of letters

parts.note: the letters run across the three words

explanation.surface: Instructions for an archaeological dig near a French castle.
explanation.definitionFit: To unearth is to dig something up from the ground, the same act as excavating.

clue.text: Louise's partner playing Hamlet

indicators.note: playing suggests performing a part loosely, so the letters of the title are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: An actress named Louise has a co-star taking the role of the Danish prince.
explanation.definitionFit: In the 1991 film Thelma & Louise, the two women are partners on the run.

clue.text: Liqueur price list outrageous — expensive, ultimately, for one

indicators.note: outrageous means wildly out of order, so the letters are rearranged
one letter stands in for another: the new letter replaces the letter meaning one

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: ultimately points to the very end of the word before it, keeping its final letter

parts.note: the final letter of expensive
I is the Roman numeral for one, the letter swapped out

explanation.surface: A drinker complains that a bar's liqueur prices are scandalously high.
explanation.walkthrough: One I in the fodder is replaced by E before the letters are rearranged. Triple sec is an orange-flavoured liqueur.
explanation.definitionFit: Triple sec is a sweet orange liqueur, so it is an example of the definition.

clue.text: Area in which pollution is controlled, not good for the kipper house?

definitions.text: Area in which pollution is controlled
definitions.meaning: first meaning: a district where burning smoky fuel is banned under clean-air rules

definitions.text: not good for the kipper house?
definitions.meaning: second, playful meaning: a kipper is a smoked herring, and a smokehouse could not operate in such a district

explanation.walkthrough: A kipper is a smoked herring; a house that cures them needs smoke, which such an area forbids. British cities created these zones under the Clean Air Acts.
explanation.definitionFit: Under British clean-air law, a designated district where only fuels that do not emit smoke may be burnt.

clue.text: English textile town, to the west a university

indicators.note: in an across entry, going west means reading right to left, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: E is the abbreviation for English
Leek is a Staffordshire town historically known for silk and textiles

explanation.surface: Describes a university town in England's textile region.
explanation.walkthrough: Keele University is in Staffordshire, a few miles from Leek.
explanation.definitionFit: Keele is a campus university in Staffordshire, so it is an example of the definition.

clue.text: Against carrying on, old Italian chap

indicators.note: to carry something is to hold it within, so one piece sits inside another

parts.note: anti means opposed to
taken as written
O is the abbreviation for old

explanation.surface: An old Italian man objecting to someone's behaviour.
explanation.definitionFit: Antonio is a common Italian man's name, so it is an example of the definition.

clue.text: Recall one hundred odd swallowing drop of special medicine?

indicators.note: to recall is to call back, so the word is read backwards
swallowing takes something inside, so one piece goes within another

parts.note: a ton is slang for one hundred

indicators.note: a drop is a tiny amount, so only the first letter of the next word is kept

parts.note: the first letter of special
rum is British slang for odd or strange

explanation.surface: Remembering a strange dose of special medicine taken a hundred times.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that a nostrum is a quack remedy rather than true medicine.
explanation.definitionFit: A nostrum is a patent remedy of dubious effectiveness, hence medicine with a question mark.

clue.text: E.g. neck ends?

parts.note: surface reading: the ends of a neck, perhaps of a bottle or garment
setter's reading: a race won by a neck is one with almost nothing between the leaders

explanation.walkthrough: In horse racing, winning 'by a neck' is a tiny margin, so a neck is an example of a tight result.
explanation.definitionFit: A race decided by a very small margin, such as a neck, is a narrow result.

clue.text: Recovering, continuously ingesting them

indicators.note: ingesting takes something into the body, so one piece is put inside another

parts.note: on end means without a break, as in hours on end
taken as written

explanation.surface: A patient gets better by taking their pills without a break.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone on the mend is getting better after illness or injury.

clue.text: Exactly how rent is paid?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: precisely, following every detail
second meaning, punning: rent goes to the person who lets the property

explanation.walkthrough: A letter here is a landlord, one who lets a property, not a written character.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means in strict accordance with the words; read literally it names the landlord who collects rent.

clue.text: Leader in Premiership, a cut above the others?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the team at the head of the football league table
second meaning: a lean joint of beef from the upper thigh, a cut that is literally from the top

explanation.walkthrough: The Premiership is the top English football league; topside is a British name for a lean beef roasting joint.
explanation.definitionFit: The leading team is the side at the top, and topside is a butcher's cut taken from the top of the leg.

clue.text: Flush? Reportedly posted a trivial amount of money

parts.note: a flush is a reddening of the face

indicators.note: reportedly means as it is said, so the following word is taken by its sound

parts.note: posted means sent by mail

explanation.surface: Someone embarrassed to have mailed only a tiny sum.
explanation.definitionFit: A red cent is an American idiom for a copper coin, hence a negligible sum.

clue.text: Doctor's entertaining chat over a brandy

indicators.note: to entertain a guest is to have them inside one's home, so one piece sits within another

parts.note: GP is a general practitioner, a family doctor
a rap is a chat or talk
taken as written

explanation.surface: A GP chatting with a patient over a glass of brandy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Over' just places the A after the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: Grappa is an Italian brandy distilled from grape pomace, so it is an example of the definition.

clue.text: Even row about card game

indicators.note: about means around, so one piece wraps around the other

parts.note: to row is to use an oar, which stands for rowing here
nap is a card game, short for Napoleon

explanation.surface: Even an argument about a game of cards.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Row' looks like a quarrel but stands for the paddle.
explanation.definitionFit: Two things on a par are equal, level or even.

clue.text: Note journalists keep back

parts.note: re is the second note of the sol-fa scale
the press is journalists collectively

explanation.surface: An instruction that reporters should withhold a memo.
explanation.definitionFit: To repress is to restrain or hold back a feeling or information.

clue.text: A group working in desert

parts.note: taken as written
a band is a group, of musicians or people
on means functioning, as a machine is on

explanation.surface: A band performing a gig out in the Sahara.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Desert' looks like a sandy place but is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To abandon is to leave someone without support, which is what deserting means.

clue.text: Some Beaujolais left in passageway

indicators.note: some means only a portion of the following words, so the solution lies inside them

parts.note: the letters run across the two words

explanation.surface: Wine has been abandoned in a corridor.
explanation.definitionFit: An aisle is a walkway between rows of seats or shelves.

clue.text: Model, keeping one's balance

indicators.note: keeping something means holding it inside, so one piece goes within another

parts.note: to model is to pose for an artist
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A catwalk model staying steady on high heels.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Keeping one's balance' reads as a single phrase, but it splits into indicator, letter and definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Poise is graceful composure or a steady equilibrium, the same as balance.

clue.text: Dissolute peer loves to get up late?

indicators.note: dissolute means loose or debauched, so the letters are loosened into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A debauched aristocrat who likes a lie-in.
explanation.definitionFit: To oversleep is to sleep past the intended time, so one rises late; the question mark marks this as a consequence.

clue.text: A boozy bender touring eastern city up north

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: touring means going around, so one piece circles another
boozy suggests drunkenness, so the letters stagger into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
E is the abbreviation for eastern

explanation.surface: A drinking spree that moves around a northern city.
explanation.walkthrough: A bender is a drinking binge. Aberdeen is a city in north-east Scotland.
explanation.definitionFit: Aberdeen is a Scottish city in the far north of Britain, so it is an example of the definition.

clue.text: Gambler in cap

definitions.meaning: second meaning: to outdo or improve on, as a verb

explanation.walkthrough: 'Cap' looks like headwear but is the verb meaning to top or surpass.
explanation.definitionFit: One who wagers is a bettor or better, and to better a performance is to cap or surpass it.
